content: Right-arm plug retention is not established by lift height, condim6 simulation success, or one successful grasp-return trial. Round2 used identical descend/grasp commands and essentially identical lift commands to a prior held trial, yet plug rotated0.9–1.0s into lift before transport. Delayed1Nm after lift cannot undo an already rotated plug. Moving1Nm transition to lift entry retained grasp and folded return in one subsequent stage trial; not stable insertion. Second independent reset with1Nm from lift retained through transport/fold, but onsite user rejected tilted carry. Native planner adds5deg preinsert tilt; absolute world/socket-axis orientation was omitted from retention-only stage criteria. An already tilted grasp can pass the change-only screen.
applicability: Current right-only original Piper task,target3,RGB-only; historical success and current failure remain distinct
count_unit: Two full-task real failures in current six-round scope; stage checks counted separately
known_limits: No accepted friction or force calibration
Qualitative real RGB posture, not metric real6DoF pose
Two stage-retention observations, transport orientation rejected, full insertion unverified.

next_checks.check: Separately verify initial absolute plug axis and transport axis; reject carry tilt even when relative in-hand pose stays unchanged. Never treat retention-only pass as full stage acceptance.
Compare current grasp/lift RGB and encoder change; reject known posture-change signature locally and fold. A pass only permits stage testing, not a physical-success label.
First inspect earlier grasp/lift phase endpoints, then first failing frame window. Compare exact commanded prefix with the closest same-scene held-stage trial before changing geometry or friction.
